run.question:
Look at the elasticsearch index 'app-278-events-n8c3v6q1': list which
fields it has (with their types), and using the index's actual field
names tell me how many documents in it are ERROR level.

report.summary: The index app-278-events-n8c3v6q1 maps exactly four fields: app (keyword), lvl (keyword), ts (date) and txt (text). There is no field named level, severity or log.level, so the level must be queried as lvl. Using the index's actual field name, documents with lvl = "ERROR" number 9 of 27 total: a term query on lvl:"ERROR" returned total 9, and a terms aggregation on lvl over the full authorized window (2026-11-20T06:53:43Z to 2026-11-21T06:53:43Z) returned buckets INFO 12, ERROR 9, WARN 6 for 27 documents. The values are uppercase; a query for lowercase "error" was not run, so whether any lowercase variants exist is unchecked (the aggregation shows no fourth bucket, with sum_other_doc_count 0, but only the three buckets were returned). The search is constrained to the ts date field; all observable documents fall between ts 2026-11-21T06:50:01Z and 2026-11-21T06:52:12Z and carry app=billing-278. The sample ERROR documents read "payment gateway timeout 1/2/3" — a log observation only, not an investigation of an incident.

claims.text: The mapping of index app-278-events-n8c3v6q1 has exactly four properties: app (keyword), lvl (keyword), ts (date), txt (text). No level/severity field exists; the severity field name is lvl.
The index app-278-events-n8c3v6q1 exists in the cluster with docs.count 27, health green, status open (state at query time 2026-11-21T06:53:45Z).

A term query {"term":{"lvl":"ERROR"}} on app-278-events-n8c3v6q1 (time field ts, window 2026-11-21T05:53:43Z to 2026-11-21T06:53:43Z) returned total 9 documents with relation eq, and a value_count aggregation on lvl over the same query returned 9.

A terms aggregation on lvl over the full authorized window (ts 2026-11-20T06:53:43Z to 2026-11-21T06:53:43Z) returned 27 matching documents with buckets INFO 12, ERROR 9 and WARN 6, doc_count_error_upper_bound 0 and sum_other_doc_count 0, so ERROR is 9 documents and no additional level bucket was reported.

The matched documents' own fields show app=billing-278 and uppercase lvl="ERROR"; the first three (sorted by ts ascending, 2026-11-21T06:50:01Z, 06:50:02Z, 06:50:03Z) have txt "payment gateway timeout 1/2/3". This is a log observation on the index, not evidence of service impact.

gaps: All ERROR-count queries are constrained to the ts date field (the tool's time filter cannot be disabled); documents with a ts outside 2026-11-20T06:53:43Z–2026-11-21T06:53:43Z would not be counted. Within that window all 27 indexed documents matched, and the observed ts values lie between 2026-11-21T06:50:01Z and 2026-11-21T06:52:12Z.

Only uppercase lvl="ERROR" was queried; no query for lowercase or other casings of the level value was run, so mixed-case variants are unchecked (the terms aggregation showed only INFO, ERROR and WARN buckets with sum_other_doc_count 0).
The mappings view is the schema at query time and does not prove which fields existing documents actually populate; only ts, lvl, app and txt were seen in the sampled documents.
No incident diagnosis was requested or performed: whether these 9 ERROR entries relate to any service fault is not established by this evidence.
next_steps: If mixed-case level values are a concern, aggregate lvl with a lowercase normalizer or query {"term":{"lvl":"error"}} against app-278-events-n8c3v6q1 to confirm none exist.

If these ERROR entries are to be treated as an incident signal, correlate the billing-278 "payment gateway timeout" texts at ts 2026-11-21T06:50–06:52 with payment-service spans and error metrics before calling anything affected.
